svg.title: KiaraDB campaign contact sheet
svg.desc: All 14 article graphics arranged in a two-column grid.

g.text: Article covers and an engine explainer.

svg.title: Automatic indexing supports changing filter combinations
svg.desc: Status, score, tags, and window fields feed a prepared store with internal indexes. Several different queries use that same store.

g.text: Prepare once. Compose conditions over searchable fields.
Automatic indexing is not index-free storage. Records and indexes occupy memory.

svg.title: Tags, dates, and ranges combined with AND
svg.desc: Three cards show required tags audited and export, a score from 80 to 95, and October 24 inside an October interval. All three feed one matching record.

g.text: Combine membership, numeric bands, and stored intervals.
Collections of disjoint intervals can contain both endpoints and still leave a gap.

svg.title: Bare values resolve to field conditions
svg.desc: The query active emea is separated into status equals active and region equals emea. If active occurs in two fields, the interface asks for a choice.

g.text: Whole-value discovery turns familiar input into explicit conditions.
If two fields contain the same value:
Ask. Then make the condition explicit.
Whole-value discovery is schema-aware, not unrestricted natural-language understanding.

svg.title: Equivalent units produce equivalent duration queries
svg.desc: time less than or equal to 500 milliseconds and duration less than or equal to 0.5 seconds both compile to duration less than or equal to 0.5 canonical seconds.

g.text: Configured conversions produce the same canonical condition.
Declare units and aliases. Store canonical values. Ask when more than one field fits.

svg.title: Typo correction preserves exact filtering
svg.desc: The misspelling serch is corrected to search. Active status and score of at least 80 are still required. One record passes; an archived and a lower-score record do not.

g.text: Forgiving words should never mean forgiving a failed filter.
Autocomplete suggests words. KeywordSearch retrieves records. Conditions enforce requirements.

svg.title: Explainable rule selection and snapshot replacement
svg.desc: Four candidate rules have specificity zero, one, one, and two. The exact rule wins. A separate pair of cards shows an active value of 40 and a prepared value of 50 before activation.

g.text: Query candidates. Define precedence. Prepare before activation.
Equal top scores? Report a tie, not a guess.
KiaraDB finds candidates. Your application owns ranking, validation, and activation.

svg.title: Schema-driven indexing and advanced filters in KiaraDB
svg.desc: A typed schema is prepared into internal indexes. Status, numeric bands, and collection requirements are composed in one query. Java and TypeScript are implementation options.

g.text: Search field combinations without manually managing composite indexes.
Java + TypeScript implementations. Prepared, in-memory data. No universal latency claim.

svg.title: DFS bounds combine two per-attribute lookups in a shared trie
svg.desc: Root spans 0 to 11. Paris spans 1 to 6, containing free 2 to 3 for hotels h1 and h2, and none 4 to 5 for h3 and h5. Rome spans 7 to 10, containing free 8 to 9 for h4. The cancellation index returns both free nodes; only the one inside Paris is kept.

g.text: No index for that pair. Just two lookups.
Simplified to two levels: city, then cancellation policy.
Is [2, 3] inside [1, 6]? Yes. Is [8, 9]? No. A few comparisons, no ID sets.
Original schematic. Bracketed numbers come from a depth-first walk, not from the data.

svg.title: Combination lookups explode while per-attribute indexes grow linearly
svg.desc: Left: one lookup per attribute combination needs 1,023 lookups for 10 attributes, 1,048,575 for 20, 1,073,741,823 for 30, and about 1.27 times 10 to the 30th for 100. Right: one index per attribute needs 10, 20, 30, and 100.

g.text: A key per attribute combination grows as 2ⁿ − 1. An index per attribute grows linearly.
Counts nonempty attribute subsets. Per-attribute indexes still use memory.

svg.title: Ten filter fields allow 1,023 combinations but need only ten per-field indexes
svg.desc: A filter panel lists ten fields, with status, score, and tags selected. Users can pick 1,023 nonempty combinations of those fields, while the application maintains only ten per-field indexes.

g.text: Index each field once. Combine the indexes at query time.
INDEXES YOU MAINTAIN, ONE PER FIELD
2¹⁰ − 1 nonempty field subsets. Per-field indexes still use memory.

svg.title: KiaraDB and Fuse.js benchmark: query latency and build time
svg.desc: Typo search over 100,000 products took 1.95 milliseconds in KiaraDB, 422 in tuned Fuse.js, and 601 in default Fuse.js. Building the indexes for the same 100,000 products took 4,286 milliseconds in KiaraDB and 266 in Fuse.js, which also used 110 MB of memory against KiaraDB's 489 MB.

g.text: Faster queries on one side, faster index builds on the other. Every exact result verified.
Memory after build: KiaraDB 489 MB, Fuse.js 110 MB
One machine, synthetic and historical data, three isolated runs. Reproduce with npm run bench:fuse.

svg.title: Introducing KiaraDB: query speed against Fuse.js
svg.desc: Typo search over 100,000 products took 422 milliseconds in tuned Fuse.js and 1.95 in KiaraDB. KiaraDB answered first-20 lists 515 times faster, stemmed search 365 times, typo search 216 times, and date equality 163 times faster. It won all 26 filter queries both libraries can run and handled 66 more that Fuse.js cannot express.

g.text: Typo search over 100,000 products. Faster in all 26 filter queries both libraries can run.
Median latency at 100,000 records, one machine, three isolated runs. Reproduce with npm run bench:fuse.

svg.title: Client-side search showdown: KiaraDB beats Fuse.js
svg.desc: A fight-card hero image for client-side search over 100,000 records. On typo search, Fuse.js took 422 milliseconds tuned and 601 with defaults; KiaraDB, crowned the winner, took 1.95 milliseconds, 216 times faster, and was up to 515 times faster on filters. A race strip shows KiaraDB finishing almost instantly while Fuse.js runs the full length. KiaraDB won 26 of 26 shared filter scenarios and ran 66 scenarios Fuse.js cannot express.

g.text: typo search, tuned · 601 ms with defaults
on typo search · up to 515× on filters
TIME TO ANSWER A TYPO SEARCH
Median latency, 100,000 records, one machine, three isolated runs · KiaraDB 1.2.0 vs Fuse.js 7.5.0 · npm run bench:fuse

svg.title: Feature comparison chart: KiaraDB and Fuse.js
svg.desc: Ticks and crosses for fourteen features. Both: exact matches across fields, typo-tolerant keyword search, and contains-any or contains-all matching on text lists. KiaraDB only: contains-any or contains-all on number lists, numeric comparisons, date and time ranges, stored ranges, missing-value filters, reported spelling corrections, a query interpreter that searches by value, and a Java edition. Fuse.js only: several typos and partial words per term, adding and removing records without a rebuild, and relevance scores with match highlighting.

g.text: Typed filters, ranges, and corrections on one side; looser fuzzy text on the other.
Search by value, no field names
From the Fuse.js 7.5.0 API and the benchmark's feature table in docs/fuse-comparison.md.
